deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is the second page of a handwritten bibliography headed on the previous page 'Vollständige Liste von Eulers Werken. Einzelne Werke' (complete list of Euler's works: separate books). The list runs chronologically from 1753 to 1785. It sits in a printed German arithmetic textbook interleaved with blank leaves; the printed §1, 'Die Arithmetik ist ein Theil der Mathematik…', is visible at the right edge.

Entries, each with place, year and format (4 = quarto, 8 = octavo):
1. Theoria motuum lunae (Berlin 1753, 4°).
2. Dissertatio de principio minimae actionis, with an examination of König's objections (Berlin, same year, 8°).
3. Institutiones calculi differentialis (Berlin 1755, 4°).
4. Constructio lentium obiectivarum ex duplici vitro (St Petersburg 1762, 4°).
5. Theoria motus corporum solidorum seu rigidorum (Rostock 1765, 4°).
6. Institutiones calculi integralis, 3 vols. (St Petersburg 1768–70, 4°).
7. Lettres à une princesse d'Allemagne, 3 vols. (St Petersburg 1768–72, 8°).
8. Vollständige Anleitung / Einleitung zur Algebra, 2 parts (St Petersburg 1770, 8°).
9. Dioptrica, 3 vols. (St Petersburg 1769–71, 4°).
10. Recherches & calculs sur l'orbite de la comète de 1769, by Lexell under Euler's direction (1770, 4°).
11. Theoria motuum lunae nova methodo pertractata (St Petersburg 1772, 4°).
12. Novae tabulae lunares (St Petersburg 1772, 8°).
13. Théorie complette de la construction & de la manoeuvre des vaisseaux (1773, 8°).
14. Instruction détaillée pour porter les lunettes au plus haut degré de leur perfection, by N. Fuss under Euler's direction (1774, 4°).
15. Éclaircissemens sur les caisses mortuaires, by N. Fuss under Euler's direction (1776, 4°).
16. Opuscula analytica (St Petersburg 1783–85, 4°).

Vertical strokes in the left margin mark three groups:
- Institutiones calculi differentialis;
- Theoria motus corporum solidorum and Institutiones calculi integralis;
- Einleitung zur Algebra and Dioptrica.
These are perhaps works the writer owned, wanted, or meant to study.

The list closely resembles the bibliographies of Euler's separately published works that circulated after his death in 1783, for example in N. Fuss's Éloge (1783/86). It was probably copied from such a printed source. Nothing on the page is derived or computed, so there is nothing to reconstruct mathematically.
errors: The first title reads 'omnes corporum inaequalitates'. Euler's actual 1753 title is 'Theoria motus lunae exhibens omnes eius inaequalitates'. The writer's 'motuum' and 'corporum' are copying slips or variants of the original title.

Minor bibliographic simplifications: the Lexell comet work's actual title includes 'la vraie orbite elliptique'. Fuss's 1776 work is titled 'Éclaircissemens sur les établissemens publics en faveur tant des veuves que des morts…'; 'caisses mortuaires' is a short form. The Algebra (1770) was published as 'Vollständige Anleitung zur Algebra'. These are abbreviations, not real errors.
The Rostock 1765 imprint of Theoria motus corporum solidorum is correct; its full imprint is Rostock and Greifswald.

results.what: Handwritten chronological list of Euler's separately published books, 1753–1785 (continuation of a list starting 1727), with marginal marks against the differential and integral calculus, rigid-body mechanics, algebra and dioptrics.
results.modern_name: Bibliography of Euler's separate works (cf. Eneström index)
results.usually_credited_to: Contemporary Euler bibliographies, e.g. N. Fuss's Éloge de M. Léonard Euler (1783); later the Eneström catalogue (1910–13)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a copied bibliography of Euler's books, with no mathematics. It is of mild biographical interest only, as possible evidence of which Euler works the young Gauss knew or sought. Gauss's early study of Euler is well documented.
transcription_corrections: The machine transcription is essentially accurate against the image. Dates 1753, 1755, 1762, 1765, 1768–70, 1768–72, 1770, 1769/70/71, 1772, 1773, 1774, 1776 and 1783–85 are all confirmed.
The first line's 'corporum' is what the manuscript shows, but it is a scribal deviation from Euler's title ('eius'). It should not be silently corrected, only annotated.

The marginal vertical strokes are not recorded in the transcription. They appear beside (a) Institutiones Calculi Differentialis, (b) Theoria motus Corporum Solidorum and Institutiones Calculi Integralis, and (c) Einleitung zur Algebra and Dioptrica.

In the next-page transcription, the 'left margin' fragments ('m inaequa…', '1753. 4.', etc.) are mirror or offset show-through of this facing page, not separate text. Its reading 'Comete de 1763' should be 1769.
